findings.reason: a node following the stated definition will either report a count it was not told to expect and look wrong, or trim to twenty and discard leaks the same plan wants fixed.
findings.text: §2's done-when requires the report to list "the twenty leaked calls" while itself defining the census as a live query (clive runs from 2026-10-20 onward, tool-use inputs containing DSML); the population grows with every new clive run, so a node dispatched later cannot produce exactly twenty. Measured today over the same window: 25 calls in 21 runs (Edit 6 and Read 4 match §1 exactly; Bash 15 against §1's 10)

findings.reason: the gate can never read clean, so a correct fix would be reported as a failure and §3 could not be closed on its own stated evidence.
findings.text: §3's closing measure is "A re-run of the census over clive runs made after the fix lands finds no leaked argument", but the census criterion is a bare substring match on the tool input, which counts a command that deliberately writes the string; the census node is itself dispatched on the local lane and its own `grep`/`python` commands that search for DSML register as leaked calls (7 of my 15 Bash hits this run)

findings.reason: §2 and §3 are separate dispatches, and without §2 handing forward a replayable artifact §3's entire done-when and its declared negative control are unmeasurable.
findings.text: §3's gate is "replaying §2's captured leaked responses through the fixed layer", and its negative control reverts the fix against those same responses, but §2 is required only to *show* the engine raw output and router block "side by side, quoted" in a report; it names no fixture path, format or capture step, so §3 may be dispatched with nothing to replay

findings.reason: §3's landing condition is a re-run of this census, so a baseline with no recorded instrument cannot be compared against, and my independent re-run already diverges from it.
findings.text: §1 states "20 of 93,862 tool calls … 10 Bash, 6 Edit and 4 Read, in 20 runs" as a completed measurement but names no command, script or log path; §2 is then told to re-run "the census below" as if it were a defined procedure

findings.reason: the answer §2 must give can establish a live defect the plan then drops, so either §3's section or a followup should hold the case explicitly.
findings.text: §2 is required both to name the markup's origin and to say whether the fig-07 truncated-path case shares that origin, a defect §1 itself says "carries no markup and may have a different cause"; if it does not share the origin, no section or followup owns it

findings.reason: the reference resolves to a census that exists and is unambiguous in context; only its direction is wrong.
findings.text: §2 refers to "the census below", but the census it means is in §1, the preceding section
